articleTitle: Velocity-Based Wind Turbine Blade Deblurring Using Richardson-Lucy Algorithm
abstract: In response to current expensive and unsafe wind turbine blade inspection techniques, alternative inspection approaches involving aerial imagery from autonomous drones and turbine blade damage-detecting machine learning algorithms have been explored. These methods require sharp, non-blurry images of wind turbine blades for accurate classification of blades as healthy or damaged. This means both current and newly explored methods can only inspect non-rotating turbines, resulting in turbine power generation losses during inspection time. To implement the proposed machine learning inspection methods during wind turbine operation hours, sharp images of the rotating turbine blades must somehow be acquired. In this research, a velocity-based Richardson-Lucy algorithm method is used to deblur aerial images of rotating wind turbine blades. This deblurring approach is first applied to artificially blurred wind turbine blade images, and then to real images of rotating turbine blades.

articleTitle: Effects of the Leaf Sheath on Stalk Strength in Maize
abstract: It has been observed that the leaf sheath of many different plants influences flexural ultimate strength. This is of particular interest for Zea mays (maize) cultivation, because the ultimate strength strongly influences the rates of brittle stalk lodging or “greensnap” failure. “Greensnap” failure in maize costs billions of dollars in lost harvests per year in the United States alone. The purpose of this study is to model the effect of the leaf sheath on the strength of maize stalks as they mature. The “DARLING” (Device for Assessing Resistance to Lodging in Grains) was used to make field measurements of stalk strength for plants with and without the leaf sheath removed. Field measurements were performed over the course of the growing season for five different Zea mays varieties. The sheath was found to have a significant effect on stalk strength. Its influence was largest for younger stalks, and became less pronounced as the stalks matured. This mirrors the effect of leaf sheath on stiffness seen in previous maize studies. The results of this study validate the need for future studies that look at how genetic and environmental factors affect the strength of maize leaf sheaths.

articleTitle: DLD Particle Separation Device with Thin Top Membrane
abstract: This study investigates the use of laminal flow mechanics of Deterministic Lateral Displacement (DLD) for particle separation. The method involves a top silicon dioxide membrane layer that facilitates control of the channel's upper layer. This approach allows future integration of other microfluidic systems involving membranes. The fabrication included a thin silicon dioxide membrane of 300 nm on top of a capillary-filled sacrificial core. Tests were performed using particles with a diameter of 2 μm to verify the flow and divergence. Results indicate the tendency of target particles to follow an expected trajectory.

articleTitle: Investigating Cyclist Injuries in Road Crashes
abstract: Cyclists often face severe injuries in collisions with vehicles. This study aimed to investigate cyclist kinematics and ground effects through the analysis of video recordings from 144 real-world crash cases. The study examined impact speeds and cyclist kinematics across all crashes, estimating vehicle impact speeds between 10 and 30 kilometers per hour. Small sedan impacts resulted in high cyclist rotation angles, with angles increasing as impact speeds rose. The most common kinematic type, forward motion, represented 42.8% of small sedan crashes and 53.8% of SUV crashes. Cyclist rotation angles and kinematics depend on the car type and impact speed. These findings offer useful insights for future research on cyclist safety.

articleTitle: Thin Membrane Hybrid Rib and Air Core ARROW Waveguides
abstract: We report the design, fabrication, and characterization of trenched hollow core anti-resonant reflecting optical waveguides (ARROWs). We discuss design principles and outline a novel fabrication process utilizing an etched trench and a thin oxide membrane. Four unique designs were created, demonstrating improved loss as ARROW layers were added. Propagation loss coefficients as low as 1 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> were measured.

articleTitle: Investigating Commuting Patterns of University Students in a High-Income Developing Country
abstract: This study explores the commuting dynamics of students at Qatar University (QU), focusing on transportation modes, demographics, and frequency of visits. The analysis reveals a predominant use of private cars, with 67% of students driving alone to campus, emphasizing the significance of individual mobility. The survey further delineates gender-based variations, particularly in the context of students commuting with chauffeurs, where 94% are female. Cultural factors play a crucial role, evident in the higher representation of Qatari nationals among students utilizing chauffeurs. While a small percentage utilizes university-provided bus services, the majority leans towards individual driving, reflecting a potential area for improvement in public transit accessibility. Overall, the findings contribute to understanding the effect of cultural, demographic, and infrastructural factors influencing students' commuting choices at QU. The implications of these insights extend to identifying policy initiatives aimed at more efficient transportation options for the university community.

articleTitle: Exploring Racial Bias in Deep Face Recognition Models
abstract: Deep convolutional neural networks (DCNNs) have played a significant role in the advancement of face recognition algorithms, demonstrating exceptional generalization capabilities on very large datasets. In the case of deep face recognition systems, models trained on racially unbalanced datasets-particularly those skewed towards majority Caucasian demographics-encounter difficulties in accurately recognizing faces from underrepresented groups. As such, this paper presents an evaluation of several state-of-the-art deep face recognition models on racially balanced datasets. The results reveal substantial performance disparities between the models on widely used benchmarks like Labeled Faces in the Wild (LFW) and unbiased datasets of comparable sizes. Of the models evaluated, FaceNet emerges as the model with the highest proficiency in generalizing across racial minorities. Emphasizing the significance of comprehensive performance reporting, we additionally advocate for metrics beyond accuracy, such as the F1 score. These additional metrics allow for derivation of new thresholds that enhance the evaluations and effectively optimize model performance across the balanced data.

articleTitle: Model-Based Reinforcement Learning with System Identification and Fuzzy Reward
abstract: An approach for model-based reinforcement learning (MBRL) gets presented utilizing system identification and fuzzy reward formulation. Minimum order estimation gets applied first to determine the system order. This aids transfer function approximation of the linear time-invariant system. A Mamdani fuzzy inference mechanism defines the reward signal. The model obtained integrates into the Q-learning process to simulate experiences bypassing the environment. The proposed framework showcases sample-efficient learning without interacting with the true system. The applicability currently limits to linear systems. Extending the techniques to nonlinear, time-varying dynamics could increase applicability to real-world systems. This paper contributes an initial demonstration of MBRL using simple dynamics approximation and fuzzy rewards. Performance analysis provides evidence of learning improvement without explicitly communicating with the actual plant. A reduction in steady state error and settling time gets achieved.

articleTitle: AI-Powered Customized University and Career Guidance
abstract: A university career decision is one of the hardest decisions that high school students must make to navigate into their academic journey. Guidance plays an important role in helping students understand the available options and shape their future. The wide variety of these available options along with the changing job market pose challenges in providing efficient guidance. Artificial intelligence (AI) can provide a solution that helps customize the university career guidance based on each student profile. The primary objective of this study is to evaluate the effectiveness of artificial intelligence in enhancing university career guidance for high school students, by providing personalized recommendations based on their academic background and preferences. The guidance is provided by introducing a web application that collects information from the student through a multi-step array of questions, providing a clear description of students' academic background and their preferences. Through integration with AI via a developed Application Programmable Interface (API) module, the tool collects information from students, and matches it to university opportunities and evolving job markets. Through this analysis, personalized career recommendations and guidance are provided to clarify different educational pathways so students can make informed decisions. This AI integration represents significant progress toward helping students with the necessary guidance to understand the most suitable educational journeys and pursue careers aligned with their preferences and capabilities. This study demonstrates the effectiveness of the studied AI-driven guidance system. By analyzing the academic and career trajectories of high school students who utilized the web application hosted as bestuniforme.com, we observed a significant improvement in their decision-making confidence and satisfaction levels. Preliminary findings suggest that students who engaged with the AI-guided system were more likely to feel confident in their university and career choices, compared to those who followed traditional guidance methods.

articleTitle: Particle Concentration and Flowrates Using Electroactuated Nanopumps
abstract: We report on a peristaltic electroactuated nanopump device made from silica. The fabrication method uses standard micro-/nanofabrication processes. Dynamic trapping of nanoparticles is reported. Particle trapping is also used to calculate fluid flowrates using fluids with known particle concentrations. Flowrates of 39fL/s/channel were measured. This rate falls to 17fL/s/channel as channels are blocked by particles.

articleTitle: Video Preprocessing for American Football Formation Recognition
abstract: American football analytics and in particular formation identification is important to gaining a competitive edge. Currently, most of this football video annotation process is done by hand. With the recent advancements in computer vision and artificial intelligence, automated sport analysis systems are gaining popularity. One major challenge in current football systems is constraints on camera location. In this work we attempt to overcome issues of camera location by performing a perspective normalization method. This entails using conventional computer vision algorithms to locate various lines and markers on the football field. This information is then used to normalize points into a camera position agnostic perspective. This preprocessing will then allow for a neural network to be trained to identify formations and preform other football analytics.

articleTitle: Charge Detection Mass Spectrometry (CDMS) of Microparticles
abstract: This paper describes a Charge Detection Mass Spectrometry (CDMS) detector for micron-sized particles and studies the effect of the detector tube diameter on the detector performance. Charged particles are measured using Image Charge Detection (ICD) and a strong electric field. Measurement results show that a reduction in the detector diameter and the introduction of a charged funnel improves the detection accuracy of single PMMA particles 5 μm in diameter.

articleTitle: Comparing Driver Behavior Along Road Sections with and without Pedestrian Crossings in a Campus Environment
abstract: This study investigates the dynamics of driver behavior in a campus environment, focusing on the influence of pedestrian crossings on speeding patterns. Speed data were collected at two Utah Valley University campus locations. The two locations included a section without pedestrian facilities and one with a marked pedestrian crossing. The speed variations based on gender and age demographics were determined. The results revealed a substantial 36% difference in the 85th percentile speeds between the two locations, with the location without pedestrian facilities exhibiting higher speeds compared to the slower speeds observed at the location with a marked pedestrian crossing. This emphasizes the role of pedestrian infrastructure in curbing speeding tendencies on shared roadways. The gender-based analysis illustrates consistent trends, with male drivers consistently exhibiting higher speeds than their female counterparts at both locations. Additionally, age-based disparities indicate complex interactions between demographic factors and speeding behaviors. Overall, the study provides valuable insights into the impact of pedestrian facilities on vehicular speeds, offering practical implications for enhancing road safety in campus environments.

articleTitle: Innovative Automatic Tool Changing Mechanism for Robotic Arms
abstract: This paper presents the development and implementation of an automatic tool-changing mechanism for industrial and collaborative robotic arms. The primary objective is to enable integration with a variety of end effectors, both active and passive, allowing the robot to autonomously switch tools without manual intervention. The system comprises three key components: a universal end-effector connector, various tools, and a customized toolbox. The universal connector will be screwed to the end of the robotic arm. It features a mechanical lock mechanism and accommodates electrical and pneumatic inlets for diverse tools. A dedicated toolbox, situated within the robot's workspace range, houses all tools for easy access. The study focuses on the design, 3D printing, and testing of two tools - an active and a passive tool - along with the innovative mechanical lock mechanism, which has been successfully developed and tested. Additionally, two industrial tasks have been defined to demonstrate the mechanism's functionality in real-world scenarios, emphasizing non-singular path trajectories between tasks. Future work includes the integration of additional sensors for enhanced automatic robot control. Overall, this research will contribute to the advancement of fully autonomous robotic systems in industrial settings.

articleTitle: Image Classification of Forest Fires Using Machine and Deep Learning
abstract: With the increasing threat presented by climate change, forest fires are becoming more destructive and frequent. These catastrophes present immense danger to our forest ecosystems, infrastructure, and overall health. To dispatch resources in a timely manner, quick and accurate identification of these fires is crucial. Here, machine and deep learning can be leveraged as a solution. In this research, we investigate the classification abilities of Support Vector Machines (SVM), Xception, ResNetSO, and MobileViT. In addition, two transfer learning approaches making use of Xception and ResNet50 as the backbone networks are explored. The popular DeepFire dataset is utilized for the training and comparison of model performance. After tuning each architecture, our results indicate the transfer learning approach with Xception as the backbone provides the highest accuracy obtaining 99.211%.

articleTitle: Source Localization Using a Single Array of Sensors in Nearfield Configuration, and Application to Active Noise Cancellation
abstract: In this paper we demonstrate by computed examples that an array of sensors in nearfield configuration can provide source localization in both <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$y$</tex>, going beyond the usual directional localization provided by a 1-dimensional array. This ability to localize a source opens new application areas. An application presented here is the possibility of doing active noise cancellation of the sound of a snorer.

articleTitle: An Analysis of Informed Search Algorithms Applied on Road Networks
abstract: Pathfinding is a complex problem with high computational costs. Yet this process is frequently used and requires high accuracy. Therefore, it is important to be able to find a highly optimal path between two points with the smallest amount of work. In this paper, we present an analysis of informed search algorithms (with an emphasis on weighted A* search) applied to pathfinding on road networks. We compare these different informed search algorithms by using randomly generated maps that emulate road networks of cities with varying road conditions like road density, speed limits, number of roads between two points, and more. After gathering all the data and statistics on the performance of these different pathfinding methods, we review the results to infer which graph search algorithms perform best in specific scenarios and in general. Based on the simulation results, we concluded that the Weighted A* search had the best performance with extremely optimal paths and low computational cost.

articleTitle: Investigating the Impact of Autonomous Vehicles on Roundabout Performance Using Microsimulation
abstract: The rise of autonomous vehicles (AVs) promises a revolution in traffic operations, due to their overall context-awareness, improved performance, and reduced crash rates. They present an ideal arena to investigate their potential impact on various traffic flow characteristics. This research investigates how increasing AVs market penetration affects operational performance at a two-lane roundabout via a microsimulation environment. Key performance measures, such as delays, number of stops, and queue length are reported. Turning movements at the studied roundabout were collected and modeled in the simulation environment to create morning and evening peak period reference cases. Five scenarios are simulated, gradually introducing AVs into the traffic stream from 0% to 30%. The results reveal significant performance improvement as the AVs penetration level increases. Delays are reduced by up to 25% at high penetration rates. This translates to substantially fewer stops and shorter queues, with reductions exceeding 30% and 50%, respectively. While this research illustrates how AVs can enhance roundabout performance and boost efficiency, its scope can be further expanded by investigating other aspects, such as safety performance, complex roundabout configurations, and high AVs market share.

articleTitle: Fabrication of High Density Flex Cables Using Direct Write Laser Ablation
abstract: Combining a “direct write” micro laser ablation process with traditional flex cable manufacturing techniques allows for the creation of low-cost, scalable, high density super-conducting flex cables with high thermal resistance. This work explores the benefits and challenges of this process and details the process used to create these cables. The process includes plating polyimide films with superconducting materials, using a femtosecond laser to create a flex cable pattern on the film and laminating several films together to create high density superconducting flex cables.

articleTitle: Strengthening Clayey Soils Using Aggregate Blending and Cement Stabilization
abstract: A key strategy employed by engineers to increase the longevity of roadways is specification of cement treatment, or stabilization, of the soil layer underlying the roadway to improve its strength and durability. Different soils require different amounts of cement to achieve the desired material properties. When a soil contains clay, an excessive amount of cement may be required to achieve the target strength. When a soil requires a high amount of cement, such as the soil studied in this research, alternative approaches are desirable because of the relatively high price of cement. One potential method of reducing the cement requirement involves the addition of crushed stone, or aggregate, to the soil. The objective of this research was to investigate the use of aggregate blending in conjunction with cement stabilization for improving the strength of a clayey soil. Samples of the clayey soil were mixed with varying amounts of cement and aggregate, compacted, cured for 7 days, and then subjected to compressive strength testing. The results indicate that an aggregate addition of 40% and a cement concentration of 5% by total dry weight of soil and aggregate can achieve a 7-day unconfined compressive strength of 3.45 MPa (500 psi), which is recommended for roadway base materials in cold regions.

articleTitle: Tiered Object Detection in Underwater Environments
abstract: This research proposes using a tiered detection pipeline to improve computer vision models that must perform across a variety of environments. The tiered pipeline classifies the environment, then uses the corresponding detection model. This method will be explored in the context of underwater navigation with different bodies of water as the varying environment. Data from the two environments is used to train models for both classification and detection, which is then compared against a single model trained on data from both environments. Comparing these two pipelines, no significant differences are apparent.

articleTitle: Automatic Regulation of Airspeed and Altitude of Aircraft Using LQR
abstract: In this work, we investigate the optimal control problem of regulating the airspeed and altitude of an airplane solely by using the elevator angle. The proposed Linear Quadratic Controller (LQR) is optimized using a Genetic Algorithm with the objective of finding the optimal weighting matrices of the optimal controller cost function. In comparison to the controllers published in other literatures, the proposed control scheme yields improved response times and magnitude.

articleTitle: Redesigning Embedded System I Course
abstract: In the rapidly changing field of embedded systems, it's imperative to continuously update and enhance educational programs to ensure they remain relevant and effective in equipping students with the necessary skills. This paper presents a revision of the ‘Embedded System I’ course at Utah Valley University. A key update is the addition of high-speed printed circuit board design, a new element compared to previous semesters. The course also integrates a deeper exploration of various memory types, enhancing the understanding of their roles in different devices. Additionally, this iteration introduces Assembly programming alongside the existing C programming labs, offering a more rounded experience in both high-level and low-level programming aspects. Feedback from students confirms the success of upgraded new topics, including interactive teaching methods, lab exercises, and a project-based learning structure, culminating in a substantial final project. These changes not only enrich the curriculum but also provide students with essential skills for success in the evolving fields of electrical and computer engineering.

Author Keywords: High-speed embedded system design on PCB

articleTitle: Power Flow Analysis Methods for Curved Shells
abstract: Curved surfaces present unique challenges in modeling and analyzing vibrations yet are essential for optimizing product designs across various industries. This paper introduces a novel approach to power flow analysis tailored for curved panels, addressing the shortcomings of traditional modeling tools. The study encompasses analytical and numerical methods, including finite element analysis and the use of Chebyshev surfaces to smooth experimental data before computing spatial derivatives. The effectiveness of the methods is demonstrated over different curvatures, loading conditions, and boundary conditions.

articleTitle: A Study on Current Travel Patterns and Anticipated Impacts of the Qatar Bahrain Causeway
abstract: This study investigates the current travel patterns and expectations of individuals commuting between Qatar and Bahrain, with a specific focus on the anticipated impact of the proposed Qatar Bahrain Causeway (QBC) on their behaviors. A diverse demographic profile, including gender, age, nationality, marital status, and income, is analyzed to provide a comprehensive understanding of the participant base shaping the study. The study explores the existing travel dynamics, modes of transportation, and purposes of travel among respondents. Using a questionnaire, the study identified the current challenges faced by commuters and their expectations regarding the QBC's potential to improve regional connectivity. The results showed that that a significant portion of respondents currently travel between Qatar and Bahrain, with a preference for air and road transport. Tourism and business were listed as primary motivations for travel. The results showed a 12% increase in the willingness to travel to Bahrain after the construction of QBC, with over 50 percent of the travelers willing to use the causeway. Participants expected reduced travel costs, shorter journey times, and increased convenience.

articleTitle: Generalized Steady-State Behavior Model for DC Wind Turbine Power and Speed Control
abstract: Wind energy has been the subject of substantial research in pursuit of renewable energy solutions. System optimization in a wind turbine requires careful control to protect mechanical elements and maximize the power delivered to an electrical load. This paper gives step-by-step procedure for modelling the steady-state behavior of DC wind turbine. Principles of the mechanical and electrical systems at play in the process of energy capture are described, and a succinct formula is derived which predicts both turbine rotational speed and the electrical power delivered to any load at any wind speed. The simplicity of this formula makes it easy to use when designing a control system to optimize power output and control the rotational speed of a turbine.

articleTitle: The Sample Rate Battle: Opposing Approaches As to Sample Rates When Digitizing Audio
abstract: The inception of widespread digitization of audio in the 1980's revolutionized the music and consumer electronics industries. This paper will empirically demonstrate some drawbacks of the industry standard sample rates for digitization of audio, and present a preliminary study comparing the status quo versus higher HD audio sample rates. Nevertheless, advocating for higher-definition digital audio through education and industry initiatives holds promise for enhancing audio experiences across digital media platforms.

articleTitle: Coding Bootcamps: Employment Outcomes
abstract: Coding Bootcamps are a relatively new phenomenon in computer science education. As such, few academic studies have assessed their effectiveness in preparing students for programming careers. Completed studies maintain a focus on the short-term results and outcomes of these programs. This paper describes a meta-analysis of multiple short-term outcomes studies and proposes the combined results as a baseline dataset for future studies. It also describes a study which gathered long-term outcomes for coding bootcamps and certificate programs and identify common factors among graduates who either successfully transitioned into software engineering, or achieved higher salaries. Lastly, it compares the long-term data to the short-term baseline dataset.

articleTitle: The Digidot: A Low-Cost, Haptic-Enabled Implementation of the Braille Writing Device
abstract: Today's technology enables a wealth of opportunities, but, oftentimes, many blind individuals are unable to benefit from these resources. Modern technology tends to rely on visual interactions, and the technologies that have been created to adapt these interactions to a non-visual medium remain prohibitively expensive. This project aims to develop a more attainable alternative so that all who are visually impaired can benefit from the digital domain. The core product is the Digidot: an electronic Perkins-layout Braille writing device that distills the core functionality of existing digital braillewriter technology along with new, innovative features into a financially accessible package. It allows characters to be input in Braille, translated to English, and transmitted to any device with which the Digidot is paired. As part of the Braille-to-English translation, an algorithm is implemented that allows consideration of user-configured abbreviations. To enable this functionality, an app was developed that allows creation and modification of abbreviations, and which syncs the abbreviations with the Digidot. This paper details the project's implementation and outcomes.

articleTitle: Fabrication of Tungsten Probe Tips on a Silicon Carbide Probe Card
abstract: This work presents a process for fabricating tungsten probe tips on a vertical silicon carbide-based probe card. The intended purpose of this device is for small-circuit assessment and verification under cryogenic temperatures. Fabrication of tungsten probe tips involves the deposition of a tungsten layer, photolithography, and wet etching. Probe tips were fabricated with heights up to 5 micrometers and diameters of between 1 and 13 micrometers.

articleTitle: Fabricating Copper Probe Tips for Vertical Probe Card Using Electroplating and Photolithography
abstract: As circuit testing becomes more complex, streamlining the fabrication of probe tips becomes increasingly valuable, especially in densely arranged arrays. This paper presents a process for fabricating copper probe tips on a vertical probe card. The technique involves creating a photoresist mold to define the shape of the tips, followed by an electroplating process. The described method offers an efficient approach to create 6μm tall copper probe tips with a tip pitch of 24μD.

articleTitle: Advancements and Insights in Autoclaved Aerated Concrete: A Comprehensive Review in Sustainable and Resilient Structural Design
abstract: This paper presents an overview of the history, structural performance, durability, resiliency, sustainability, and construction of autoclaved aerated concrete (AAC). The primary strengths of AAC are its thermal performance, fire resistance, versatility in construction, and other lightweight properties. Some potential challenges with autoclaved aerated concrete include its naturally lower strength and permeability, making it important to consider water penetration issues. Other properties of AAC are discussed, and future work is included.

articleTitle: Improving Malware Detection from Binary Control Flow Graphs Using Supervised Learning
abstract: Malware is a persistent threat to cybersecurity which makes its early detection crucial. This paper is built on previous work where a pipeline was built to convert program files from binaries to data forms that can be used to classify them as malicious or benign. The pipeline begins by reading in program binary files initially known to be benign or malicious into graphs which are then converted to sparse and dense vector representations. Supervised machine learning models are then utilized to measure and compare their efficacy when identifying malware from varying vector types and are compared to baseline accuracy measurements gathered from unsupervised learning methods.

articleTitle: A Comparison of Many Approaches to Solving the Multiple Traveling Salesman Problem
abstract: The Multiple Traveling Salesman Problem (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$mTSP$</tex>) is a canonical problem in multi-agent coordination, and many approaches to solving this problem have been developed over the years. An evaluation of several approaches to solving the multi-depot multiple traveling salesmen problem, including Genetic Algorithms, Ant Colony Optimization, and multiple Market-Based approaches are given. Ant Colony Optimization techniques tend to reach closer to optimality, while market-based techniques produce results very quickly.

articleTitle: Distress Surveys of Pavement Panel and Bridge Deck Areas Repaired Using Rapid-Setting Concrete Batched in a Volumetric Concrete Mixer
abstract: Repairs of concrete pavement panels and bridge decks in Utah are commonly performed using rapid-setting concrete to expedite the concrete curing process and thereby minimize the impacts of lane closures on traffic. The objective of this research was to perform distress surveys of several pavement panel and bridge deck areas repaired using rapid-setting concrete to evaluate the apparent durability of in-service repairs. The scope of work included documenting the occurrence of cracking, scaling, spalling, delamination, and construction issues at each of six sites in northern Utah, where rapid-setting concrete placements batched using volumetric concrete mixers had been in service for 4 to 5 years at the time of inspection. The results of the distress surveys indicate that, for the rapid-setting concrete repairs evaluated in this study, cracking and scaling were observed to be the most prevalent and extensive distresses. Therefore, improvements in the durability of the rapid-setting concrete are needed to especially address cracking and scaling. Aspects of both mixture design and construction should be considered to reduce the occurrence of damage and extend the service life of rapid-setting concrete repairs in cold regions.

articleTitle: Wind Turbine Classification for Autonomous Inspection: A Case Study Using Deep Learning
abstract: Recent developments in drone technology facilitate wind turbine inspection with lower downtime, cost, and health risk. The typical method of drone inspection, however, requires a certified pilot to manually fly the drone around the wind turbines being inspected. In pursuit of creating a fully autonomous drone system for inspecting wind turbines, this paper evaluates three deep learning architectures for the task of wind turbine classification’ which means determining whether an RGB image contains wind turbines. In the eventual autonomous drone system, this visual feedback will enable the drone to confirm it has reached the wind turbine rather than only relying on GPS, which has a degree of uncertainty. This research focuses on implementing and tuning the VGG19, ResNet50, and Xception convolutional neural networks to achieve high accuracy at this task. The outcomes are described in this paper along with the dataset created to train and test the networks.

articleTitle: Q-Learning Based Control for Swing-Up and Balancing of Inverted Pendulum
abstract: This study addresses the classic control problem of stabilizing an inverted pendulum on a moving cart, a challenge in control theory and robotics due to its inherent instability and highly nonlinear dynamics. We explore the application of Q-learning, a model-free reinforcement learning algorithm, and its efficacy in deriving an optimal control policy for the system without precise system models. Our approach utilizes Q-learning's capacity for stabilizing a pendulum in an upright position on the top of the horizontally moving cart within a certain boundary. Our strategy adapts to a dynamic environment while showcasing its robustness in developing control policies for complex systems. This research bridges classical control theory with reinforcement learning techniques, contributing to the domain by demonstrating the versatility and potential of machine learning in control tasks.

articleTitle: White-Label Bootcamps: Branding and Opinions
abstract: Coding bootcamps have become a common education option within the United States. Two organizations, Fullstack Academy and EdX, have each developed a white-label bootcamp program marketed through partnering universities. Because these bootcamps offer their services under the name of their university partners, the public likely misunderstands the nature of the bootcamps, mistaking them as university programs. We conducted a study to gather public opinion, identifying whether these misunderstandings exist, and if they have created biases based on university rankings. Our study also sought to identify whether there is public bias favoring university-affiliated coding bootcamps over traditional coding bootcamps. We find that most individuals rank these program offerings as equal. However, a portion of bootcamp participants revealed a preference for higher-ranked universities over lower-ranked universities, even when the white-label bootcamp was the same for both. A similar portion of the general population displayed a preference for university-affiliated bootcamps over traditional bootcamps.

articleTitle: Near-Field Magnetic Loop Antenna for Fetal Cardiac Monitoring Initial Explorations
abstract: This article is the start of a series that describes the development of a near-field magnetic loop antenna for fetal cardiac monitoring. This first installment describes the device, theory of operation, and initial sensitivity to fluid depth in a saline tank model using S11 parameters. Two modes of operation are described: uniform current and resonant mode.

articleTitle: Roughening of SU8 Waveguides to Accentuate Light Scattering
abstract: In this study, we investigate a technique for roughening the surface of multi-mode-interference (MMI) waveguides so that interference modes can be more easily imaged. The MMIs are constructed on silicon substates using SU8, a photodefineable polymer that has low absorption of visible light and a refractive index of 1.59. We find that exposing the SU8 to an O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> plasma in a reactive ion etcher creates a surface layer of nanoscopic grass which is efficient at scattering light.

articleTitle: Revisiting Plagiarism Deterrence in CS1 Through Keystroke Data
abstract: The following paper addresses student attitudes towards keystroke logging and plagiarism prevention measures. Specifically, the paper concerns itself with changes made to the “ShowYourWork” plugin, which was implemented to log the keystrokes of students in Utah State University's introductory Computer Science course, CS1400. Recent work performed by the Edwards Lab provided insights into students' feelings towards keystroke logging as a measure of deterring plagiarism. As a result of that research, we decided to investigate how students' perception of keystroke logging and plagiarism changes when they are given more control over their data. This paper introduces the work done to enhance student privacy and feelings of security and an evaluation of the effectiveness of the changes made to ShowYourWork.

articleTitle: Addressing the Challenge of Missing Medical Data in Healthcare Analytics: A Focus on Machine Learning Predictions for ICU Length of Stay
abstract: This research investigates the impact of missing data on the performance of machine learning algorithms, with a particular focus on the MIMIC-IV dataset. This project aims to investigate the extent to which missing data negatively impacts the training of machine learning algorithms, and whether demographic groups with a higher proportion of missing data (i.e.,ethnicity) have lower predictive accuracy. Using advanced machine learning and data analysis techniques, our results highlight important considerations related to missing data in medical datasets and provide useful insights for improving predictive modeling and decision support systems in clinical practice offers.

articleTitle: Early-Age Stiffness and Strength of Concrete Comprising Natural Pozzolans Available in Utah
abstract: Renewed interest in the use of natural pozzolans in concrete in Utah has led to new research, in which the properties and performance of locally available natural pozzolans are being evaluated in selected concrete mixtures. The objective of this laboratory research was to determine the 7-day stiffness, in terms of modulus of elasticity, and compressive strength of concrete mixtures comprising natural pozzolan for comparison with a baseline concrete mixture without natural pozzolan. For all three natural pozzolans evaluated in this research, both slump and air content requirements were met at the maximum water-cementitious materials ratio of 0.44 permitted by the Utah Department of Transportation. The results indicate average modulus of elasticity values ranging from 11,278 MPa (1,635,744 psi) to 11,665 MPa (1,691,867 psi) for mixtures comprising natural pozzolan compared to a modulus of elasticity value of 12,346 MPa (1,790,667 psi) for the baseline mixture. The results also indicate average compressive strength values ranging from 24.1 MPa (3498 psi) to 28.8 MPa (4183 psi) for mixtures comprising natural pozzolan compared to a compressive strength value of 33.1 MPa (4795 psi) for the baseline mixture. This research is expected to enhance understanding of natural pozzolan use in concrete mixtures in Utah projects.

articleTitle: Flashing Stop Signs vs. Traditional Stop Signs: An Investigation into Driver Compliance at All-Way Stop-Controlled Intersections
abstract: This study aims to assess the effectiveness of flashing stop signs compared to traditional non-flashing stop signs. Four locations were selected for data collection, covering both daytime and evening periods. Two locations featured flashing stop signs, while the other two had traditional non-flashing stop signs. Collected data included drivers' gender, ethnicity, age, vehicle type, intersection conditions upon approach, and stop behavior-whether they came to a complete stop, executed a rolling stop, or did not stop at all. The analysis revealed a higher rate of complete stops at intersections with flashing stop signs compared to those without. Additionally, fewer rolling stops occurred at intersections with flashing signs compared to traditional non-flashing signs.

articleTitle: Analyzing Differential Impact of Text-Based Instructions in Video Games
abstract: While designing a video game, the first priority of game developers is to create an ultimate source of fun and entertainment. Even though the proper design of game rules and the placement of game challenges are crucial to achieving this goal, teaching players how to navigate and interact with them is pivotal. Instructions or tutorials embedded in video games, especially in serious games are essential to achieve the targeted goal successfully. In this experiment, we designed and developed a 2D game to explore whether different formats of text-based instructions integrated into the gameplay have a unique influence on players' performances as well as game experiences. Three identical versions of the game were developed except for the layout of the text-based instruction. Our experimental outcome demonstrated that simpler layouts are more effective in providing players with a better overall experience.

articleTitle: Comparative Empirical Analysis of Dancing Links Implementations to Solve the Exact Cover Problem
abstract: Understanding and efficiently solving NP-complete problems remains a fundamental challenge in computational theory (CT). This paper presents XD, a modified Dancing Links algorithm (DLX) that solves the NP-complete exact cover problem. We implement the algorithm using dictionaries and compare this implementation against a more traditional implementation that uses matrices to assess cases in which each implementation performs best. One of the key strengths of the modified algorithm is its simplicity and adaptability. Our implementation is included in Redux, an online, interactive, dynamic knowledgebase of NP-complete problems, reductions, and solution algorithms.

articleTitle: Advancing Understanding: Welded Wire Reinforcement Use in Concrete Structures
abstract: This paper aims to assess the current state of knowledge regarding welded wire reinforcement (WWR). Over the years, WWR has undergone extensive testing to enhance understanding of its properties and performance as a reinforcement material. Historically, concerns have centered around the ductility of WWR. Recent code revisions, aimed at bolstering ductility requirements for non-prestressed steel reinforcement, have raised concerns within the industry. While these code updates currently do not encompass WWR, this review serves to provide preliminary insights to support ongoing research endeavors. By elucidating the current state of WWR, this review seeks to prepare for the potential expansion of these code requirements to include WWR alongside non-prestressed reinforcement materials.

articleTitle: Secrecy and Resilience in Next-Gen Wi-Fi: Exploring a Multi-User Down-Link Non-Orthogonal Transmission Framework
abstract: Next-generation Wi-Fi communication necessitates improved spectral efficiency, low latency, expanded coverage, robustness, and enhanced communication security. A major challenge in current and future Wi-Fi communication is preventing eavesdroppers from intercepting live transmissions and ensuring enhanced communication secrecy. The non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) scheme has emerged as a potential candidate for future Wi-Fi communication. This is attributed to its notable characteristic of serving multiple users simultaneously on the same time/frequency resources. In this work, my motivation is to propose a novel NOMA transmission scheme that can serve multiple users without any information leakage to an internal or external eavesdropper. My proposed NOMA transmission scheme utilizes physical layer security (PHY) and is less complex, more efficient, and more robust than the conventional power domain NOMA (PD-NOMA) transmission. PD-NOMA suffers from various drawbacks, such as the use of successive interference cancellation (SIC), which demands power sharing among users and has a high probability of information leakage

articleTitle: Transit Stops in a Developing Country: Unraveling Challenges and Complexities
abstract: Transit stops play a key role in the public transport system. If designed properly, it can attract more people to public transport. Carefully planned and appropriately built transit stops facilitate integration between different modes of public transport, allow passengers to safely access public transportation, and reduce the effort required to access transit. The purpose of this work is to highlight certain challenges and issues associated with existing transit stops in a developing country, recognizing that these are special cases. The findings of this work can inform future transit stop designs and policies, ultimately improving public transportation efficiency and user experience.

articleTitle: Generative AI Adoption in the Classroom: A Contextual Exploration Using the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and the Innovation Diffusion Theory (IDT)
abstract: The burgeoning development of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) and the widespread adoption of large language models (LLMs) in educational settings have sparked considerable debate regarding their efficacy and acceptability. Despite the potential benefits, the assimilation of these cutting-edge technologies among educators exhibits a broad spectrum of attitudes, from enthusiastic advocacy to profound skepticism. This study aims to dissect the underlying factors influencing educators' perceptions and acceptance of GenAI and LLMs. We conducted a survey among educators and analyzed the data through the frameworks of the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and Innovation Diffusion Theory (IDT). Our investigation reveals a strong positive correlation between the perceived usefulness of GenAI tools and their acceptance, underscoring the importance of demonstrating tangible benefits to educators. Additionally, the perceived ease of use emerged as a significant factor, though to a lesser extent, influencing acceptance. Our findings also show that the knowledge and acceptance of these tools is not uniform, suggesting that targeted strategies are required to address the specific needs and concerns of each adopter category to facilitate broader integration of AI tools in education.

articleTitle: Concrete Mixture Properties and Designs for Additive Manufacturing: A Review of 3D Concrete Printing
abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) concrete printing has emerged as a promising technology for revolutionizing construction practices, offering unparalleled flexibility and efficiency in building complex structures. However, the successful implementation of 3D concrete printing relies heavily on the development of appropriate mixture designs tailored to the unique requirements of additive manufacturing. This paper presents a comprehensive review of mixture properties critical for successful 3D concrete printing, including pumpability, extrudability, and constructability, and summarizes published concrete mixtures tailored for optimal 3D printing performance. Key aspects of the mixture designs include water-cement ratio, fly ash, silica fume, superplasticizers and viscosity-modifying agents, and fibrous additions. This paper serves as a valuable resource for researchers, engineers, and practitioners involved in 3D concrete printing, fostering continued innovation and refinement in mixture design methodologies to advance the adoption of this transformative construction technology.

articleTitle: Advanced Mobility: Integrating Visible Light Communication and Sensing Technologies
abstract: Visible Light Communication (VLC) is an emerging technology that has gained significant attention in recent years due to its immense potential for transforming transportation systems. VLC enables short-range high-speed, secure, and reliable vehicle-to-vehicle and vehicle-to-infrastructure communication in various use cases. This work delves into compelling applications of VLC in transportation, highlighting its unique advantages over traditional communication technologies. Leveraging high-speed, secure, and reliable vehicle and vehicle-to-infrastructure communication, VLC offers unprecedented opportunities for enhancing road safety, traffic management, and overall transportation efficiency.

articleTitle: Optimized Two-Stage Scheduling for Electric Vehicle Charging: A Machine Learning Approach
abstract: As the adoption of Electric Vehicles (EVs) continues to increase worldwide, efficient management of EV charging schedules appears as a crucial challenge. This paper proposes a two-stage optimization approach for the scheduling of EV charging, aiming to predict vehicle departure time, allocate maximum power while considering uncertainty, customer satisfaction and profit of the EV charging stations. At first, the model uses machine learning model: Xgboost to predict EV departure time. This is done by training the machine learning model on unique dataset consisting of real historical data. From the departure data, two stage optimization is solved. The first stage is solved using the Monte Carlo Based method by solving different scenarios and taking the average of all the scenarios to find the expected grid power. The second stage involves realtime optimization for power allocation, focusing on cost reduction and a priority-based power allocation while incorporating power data from the first stage. From the two different case studies, the station profit was found to be $ 96.70 and $ 77.94 for 10 vehicles respectively. Also, grid impact analysis was carried out on IEEE-34 distribution system. Overall, our research contributes practical insights for the intelligent scheduling of EV charging, facilitating a sustainable shift towards green transportation.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Analysis on Gunshot Recognition
abstract: The ability to recognize a gunshot has significance in reinforcing public safety, assisting in crime scene investigations, and preventing gun violence. This paper investigates the efficiency of various machine learning models for gunshot recognition. We present a model to identify the type of pistol or rifle discharged by analyzing only an audio signal of the gunshot. Among the array of methods explored, AdaBoost performed the best achieving an accuracy of 99.9% and sustaining over 80% accuracy with 40 dB conditions. Additionally, we experimented with the importance level of the features to identify the most relevant variables that boost the performance of the algorithms.

articleTitle: Design and Kinematic Analysis of an Aerial Robotic Arm for Precision Agriculture
abstract: This paper presents the design and kinematic analysis of a novel aerial unmanned robotic arm with integrated storage, termed AURAS, aimed at enhancing agricultural efficiency. Focusing on the challenges of integrating robotic arms with unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), particularly for agricultural applications, it proposes a lightweight, compact design with minimal actuation requirements. The AURAS design features a foldable arm mechanism allowing for the extension, retraction, and gripping of objects, combined with onboard storage to minimize the need for frequent returns to base. Through kinematic analysis, including mobility, limit angles, and forward kinematics, the paper demonstrates the feasibility of the design. It concludes with future research directions aimed at refining the mechanism's design and operational reliability for practical agricultural use.

articleTitle: Integrating Satellite Imagery and Infield Sensors for Daily Spatial Plant Evapotranspiration Prediction: A Machine Learning-Driven Approach
abstract: Continuous monitoring of crop health, especially plant EvapoTranspiration (ET) helps make efficient irrigation decisions. While various infield and remote sensing technologies provide valuable data, challenges lie in obtaining fine-resolution spatiotemporal observations. Moreover, existing research primarily addresses gap-filling past data, limiting the potential for advanced irrigation practice optimization tethered to historical observation-based management. Our work enables preemptive irrigation management by predicting the spatial ET on a day-ahead basis. We implement a Machine Learning (ML)-driven method, named Data Fusion Using Satellite and Infield Observations for Neural-network-based prediction of spatiotemporal plant EvapoTranspiration (DFUSIONET). This methodology in-cludes an Earth Observation (EO) based spatial ET-generation model, a unique interpolation method named Proportional-offset Interpolation (POI) for temporal gap-filling, and a multi-input Feedforward Neural Network (FNN) for predicting daily spatial ET. Results demonstrate that the POI method outperforms other interpolation techniques with an RMSE of 0.11 mm d-<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>, and the FNN exhibits a RMSE range of [0.13, 0.31] mm d<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>.DFUSIONET integrates satellite imagery, infield sensor data, and meteoro-logical parameters and captures spatiotemporal variations of site-and crop-specific parameters to predict plant ET. This forecasting strategy is beneficial for efficient preemptive irrigation management, contributing to sustainable agricultural practices and improved resource utilization in precision agriculture.

articleTitle: Utilizing Augmented Reality for Upper-Extremity Prosthesis Dimensioning
abstract: Augmented Reality (AR) with the assistance of myoelectric sensors has been shown to be a powerful tool in virtual rehabilitation for trans-radial arm amputees. Current methods utilize a pre-dimensioned and fabricated virtual prosthetic inside of the AR space to allow users to practice controlling a virtual prosthetic. This practice is in preparation for daily activities while using the prosthetic device. Understanding the potential that AR has in shaping the rehabilitation process, we aim to investigate whether this potential can carry over in the fitting process of the prosthetic device, i.e., the dimensioning of the prosthesis and its accuracy down to the millimeter level. To accurately obtain the dimensions necessary for the creation of an upper-extremity prosthetic an AR application is developed and launched through Microsoft's HoloLens 2 headset. The proposed method uses grabbable virtual markers that assist in obtaining the measurements and dimensions of a virtual prosthetic. The sensitivity and accuracy of the application is analyzed across usage from multiple participants with the mean average error generally ranging from 1–2 mm.

articleTitle: Archaeoastronomy at the Byzantine Church Complex at Ḥorvat Beit Loya
abstract: This study investigates the astronomical alignments of the Byzantine church complex at Ḥorvat Beit Loya in Israel to understand its orientation and cultural significance. The site's historical context, proximity to pilgrimage routes, and church's function as a Christian center are outlined. Through archaeoastronomical research, potential alignments with celestial phenomena and religious festivals are identified. The findings suggest a significant alignment with the sunrise on the feast day of St. James the Apostle which indicates the possibility of the church being dedicated to him. The study reveals the intricate relationship between architecture, astronomy, iconography, and culture in Byzantine Christianity.

articleTitle: Digital Design Education Using an Open-Source, Cloud-Based FPGA Toolchain
abstract: Digital design tools typically have a high barrier to entry: setup is challenging for beginners, and installation often requires a high-performance workstation. In this work, we present an educational framework for digital design using cloud-based resources and open-source tools. We leverage Google Colab notebooks to allow users to run FPGA simulation and design tools remotely, using only a simple web browser. The tools are capable of running simulations with visualizations, and can generate FPGA bitstreams for commercial devices. In addition, we have developed several notebook-based labs to teach digital design topics, including arithmetic, combinational and sequential circuits, and FSMs.

articleTitle: Mission Planning and Execution Architecture for Robotic Systems Using BPMN
abstract: Multi-robot systems need expressive and adaptive mission modeling and execution architectures that general users can understand. This paper develops a mission modeling and execution architecture that provides expressive modeling capabilities via the Business Process Modeling Notation (BPMN). Flexible and dynamic mission execution is combined with dynamic resource allocation. The architecture is demonstrated via the simulation of a surveillance mission where several robots must visit and investigate many locations. The surveillance mission highlights key aspects of the expressibility and adaptability of the architecture.

articleTitle: Assessing LWIR and Visual Sensor Modalities for UAV Detection and Tracking
abstract: The development of unmanned aerial vehicles has led to a proliferation of drones being used for many different tasks. This necessitates systems for preventing collisions and other accidents, as well as malicious activities that could be carried out by drone operators. A vital part of that task is detecting and tracking drones. Different sensors have different strengths and weaknesses, so it is likely that a combination of sensors will be used in future systems. In order to facilitate the design of such systems, the limitations of current sensors and methods should be assessed. Here, the limitations of single-frame LWIR and RGB camera data are analyzed. Deep learning methods are applied to data at different ranges of pixels-on-target. The given results document the relative success of current single-frame detection methods on these drone targets.

articleTitle: Wind Turbine Blade Fault Detection via Thermal Imaging Using Deep Learning
abstract: This research focuses on leveraging fusion imaging, which combines thermal and RGB data, for the inspection of Wind Turbine Blades. We introduce a novel dataset comprising 1000 fused images of a Primus Air Max wind turbine and analyze it using advanced deep learning models including AlexNet, VGG, ResNet, Xception, and DenseNet. Among these, DenseNet emerges as the superior model, demonstrating exceptional capability in detecting defects in WTBs. DenseNet's architecture, characterized by its dense connectivity pattern that ensures each layer is directly connected to all subsequent layers, significantly enhances feature extraction and reduces false negative rates. This makes it an ideal choice for automating and improving the accuracy of wind turbine maintenance processes.

articleTitle: Microphone Placement for Sparse 2D Beamforming Arrays
abstract: Presented in this paper is a method for determining the optimal microphone positions for a two-dimensional (2D) beamforming array, which will be referred to as the average-gain microphone placement (AMP) method. The AMP method is specifically intended for applications where an undesired sound (noise) is expected to come from a single direction and desired sound is expected to come from a range of directions. The optimum placement determined by the algorithm yields the best average performance over the range of anticipated directions of arrival, rather than the best performance in any single direction. The AMP method notably includes a procedure for reducing the performance characteristics of an array to a single-valued performance metric, which allows for a definitive optimum to be located. A typical application would be for filtering speech with a large noise source in a single direction, such as machinery or HVAC equipment. Both the optimization routine and the method for predicting performance can be applied to 2D microphone arrays of any size. Results that demonstrate the validity of both the optimization and performance predictive methods are shown and discussed.

articleTitle: The Water Quality Smart Monitor: A Cost-Conscious Approach for Personal Water Testing
abstract: As concerns over water quality escalate, there is an increasing need for efficient and user-friendly methods of assessing water. This paper introduces a water quality monitoring system utilizing a suite of sensors, including oxidation-reduction potential (ORP), turbidity, total dissolved solids (TDS), pH, temperature, and image capture. Most water monitoring devices cost tens of thousands of dollars and are complicated to use. The primary objective is to empower users with an affordable and simple yet effective tool for on-the-spot water quality assessment. The system employs multiple probes, designed to be submerged into a water sample. The collected data is seamlessly transmitted to a smartphone app through wireless connectivity. The app interprets the sensor data and provides users with intuitive feedback on water quality, offering insights into parameters crucial for assessing potability and environmental impact. Key features of this work include realtime monitoring, ensuring rapid detection of water quality in fresh samples, and an easy-to-use interface that requires minimal user input. The integration of image capture with a support vector machine (SVM) adds a visual component, detecting potential contaminants in the water. The smartphone app serves as a user-friendly platform for displaying and interpreting the collected data, making water quality assessment accessible to individuals without specialized knowledge in the field. While a few improvements are necessary to enhance its commercial viability, such as replacing the turbidity sensor, this prototype serves as a proof of concept that water quality assessments can be conducted simply and at a low cost.

articleTitle: Quantum-Accelerated Nash Equilibrium Search for Optimal Relay Selection in Wireless Networks
abstract: In wireless networks, optimizing relay selection is crucial for enhancing efficiency and improving user experience. Traditional methods often struggle to adapt to dynamic network conditions, leading to sub-optimal performance. Nash Equilibrium, where no user can unilaterally improve its Quality of Experience (QoE), offers a stable solution but is computationally demanding, especially in large networks. To address this challenge, we propose a novel approach leveraging quantum computing techniques, specifically quantum game theory, to efficiently achieve Nash Equilibrium in relay selection. Our method promises significant reductions in computational complexity while offering more robust and optimal relay selection strategies. By capturing the intricate dynamics of relay selection using quantum mechanics, we aim to advance network optimization and improve overall performance. Potential applications include scenarios where rapid adaptation to changing network conditions is essential for maintaining high-quality communication.

articleTitle: Differentially Flat Model Predictive Trajectory Tracking for Mobile Robots
abstract: This work presents a model-predictive, trajectory-following strategy for mobile robot navigation. Given a path to be followed, a trajectory can be formed using numerous techniques ranging from interpolation to smoothing. A trajectory-tracking controller can then be employed. Smoothing the path over its entirety while considering vehicle motion constraints is computationally prohibitive while interpolation techniques may be insufficiently smooth to avoid undesirable transient effects when there are sharp changes in path direction. Thus, a model predictive control (MPC) technique is employed to smooth the trajectory for a small amount of time in front of the current position of the vehicle. The model used within the predictive controller is a differential flat representation of the robot dynamics. This enables quadratic programming techniques to be employed for the rapid creation of the nonlinear robot trajectory. The differentially flat state resulting from the MPC is passed to a trajectory tracking controller capable of tracking a differentially flat trajectory. Thus, the MPC essentially iteratively reshapes the trajectory to account for the motion constraints of the vehicle. Simulation examples are provided to demonstrate the ability of the receding horizon framework to respect vehicle dynamics while creating a reference trajectory that compensates for a non-smooth desired path.

articleTitle: Development of a Bio-Inspired Microfluidic Valve
abstract: While microfluidic devices have provided numerous breakthroughs in analysis of biological and other samples and are useful in wearable biosensors, continuous passive pumping in micro fluidic devices remains a difficult challenge. This work documents the development of a 20:1 scaled prototype biomimetic micro fluidic device patterned after physiological valves such as those found in lymphatic vessels and some deep veins, which harness fluid pressure oscillations caused by movement of surrounding tissue to provide for distributed passive pumping. Basic functionality of the valve is demonstrated, including opening and closing with pressure gradient oscillations to allow for forward flow and prevent backward flow, giving a net forward pumping effect. Preliminary experimental results are compared to previous numerical findings. The scaled prototype device demonstrates that such a device can in fact be created and can harness fluid pressure fluctuations to provide pumping. This device provides a groundwork for further miniaturization to provide distributed passive pumping in microfluidic devices such as wearable biosensors. Further, the scaled device can be used to provide physiologically-relevant conditions for in-vitro study of cell behavior.

articleTitle: Load Balanced Handover Planning for LEO Satellite Communication Networks
abstract: To ensure uninterrupted service for a user, frequent handovers are essential in a LEO satellite network. Since satellites follow predictable orbits, the movement pattern of a satellite is deterministic. Exploiting the predictability of satellite locations, we devise a handover scheduling plan that incorporates load balancing considerations in satellite networks. To reduce computational complexity, we organize users in close proximity into groups and formulate handover planning based on these user groups. We approach the problem by treating it as a routing problem in an auxiliary graph, which represents the candidate satellites capable of providing qualified connectivity for a user group. We formulate the handover planning problem as two concatenated Integer Linear Programming (ILP) problems. The objective function of the first problem aims to minimize the traffic on the most heavily loaded satellite. The load on the most congested satellite, obtained from the first problem, serves as a constraint in the second problem. This constraint is employed to set an upper limit on the load for each satellite. The objective function of the second problem is to minimize the total number of handovers. The numerical results demonstrate that our approach significantly reduces the load on the most congested satellite compared to methods that use signal strength and longest service time as handover criteria. Our handover planning results in only a slight increase in the total number of handovers compared to the longest service time strategy.

articleTitle: Material Selection for a Custom Chassis Design
abstract: Virtual prototype simulation and analysis, based on 3D modeling software is a high-efficiency and low-cost product development model. The design and testing of the mechanical properties and material selection of a custom autonomous ground vehicle (AGV) chassis for environments with rugged terrains like forests is discussed in this paper. This research tests the capabilities of the chassis to endure subjected loads in its challenging operating environment. The 3D design is built in SolidWorks® and the static structural analysis is performed. This paper also compares other research endeavors in the realm of chassis design, focusing on factors such as maximum stress, and deflection of critical sections under diverse loading conditions. The design constraints of focus were a reduction of weight, efficient material utilization, and minimizing cross-sectional dimensions. Simulation techniques were employed to narrow the best-performing materials for our chassis. The outcomes of this study encompass a well-founded chassis design achieved through stress analysis, safety factor analysis, and chassis deflection analysis. The analysis results identify material for the custom chassis to endure shocks, torsional forces, vibrations, and other operating stresses.

articleTitle: Autonomous Surveillance Breakthrough by Implementing Facial Recognition in Dog Robots
abstract: As the importance of security in today's world continues to escalate, technology's role in its enhancement has evolved significantly. From the inception of fixed security cameras monitored by individuals, advancements have steered towards autonomous threat recognition systems and the deployment of mobile robots for proactive security measures. Despite these technological strides, the exploration of autonomous robots in security has been relatively scant. This study takes a novel approach by repurposing the commercial GO2 Edu dog robot for security purposes, equipping it with a thermal camera and custom software for robust face detection in varying lighting conditions, aimed at achieving safer and more reliable face recognition. Furthermore, the mapping and navigational capabilities are studied by conducting experiments with a Turtlebot outfitted with a 2D RPLIDAR and depth camera using SLAM, laying the groundwork for the GO2 robot's autonomous operations. The results of these enhancements have shown to be promising in the context of bolstering security measures. The paper concludes with a discussion on potential future enhancements, paving the way for more sophisticated and autonomous security robots.

articleTitle: Tire-Pavement Interface Noise: Mechanisms and Mitigation
abstract: Among the many contributors to pavement noise, tire-pavement interface noise (TPIN) plays a significant role. Although considerations of pavement noise are often overlooked during pavement design and construction, the expansion of transportation networks within cities warrants designing and maintaining quieter pavements to reduce TPIN. The objectives of this research are to explain noise-generation and noise-reduction mechanisms, describe pavement noise mitigation practices, and propose further research on these topics. TPIN can be caused by aerodynamic, vibro-dynamic, and adhesion mechanisms. Noise-reduction mechanisms (NRMs) are methods by which the amplitude and intensity of sound can be reduced. When applied to pavements, NRMs can be categorized as porous sound absorption, resonance sound absorption, connected pore excretion, control of sound propagation path, and damping. Specific types of pavements can be used to mitigate TPIN. However, the most common pavement noise prevention method is the application of a properly designed noise-reducing wearing course (NRWC). Three areas recommended for further research include using recurring cleanings over time for unclogging pores in NRWCs, methods of preventing or reducing aging of asphalt while preserving the noise-reduction properties of NRWCs, and the utilization of porous ultra-thin overlays.

articleTitle: Airtightness Performance of Thin-Shell Concrete Dome Structures
abstract: In response to the urgent need to mitigate greenhouse gas emissions and enhance energy efficiency in residential buildings, this research paper evaluated an insulated concrete thin-shell dome structure for airtight-ness. Residential buildings are significant contributors to global emissions, with heating and cooling systems being the primary culprits. Airtightness is identified as a key factor in improving energy efficiency and reducing emissions. The paper integrates existing research in concrete thin-shell domes and modular structures, focusing on airtightness strategies within modular construction. Methods include experimental testing using the blower door test to evaluate airtightness. Results demonstrate optimal airtightness performance in a concrete dome structure, surpassing regulatory requirements. The study highlights the effectiveness of modular construction methodologies in achieving superior airtightness, thereby enhancing overall building performance and energy efficiency.

articleTitle: Index
